Chapter 1: Life Before Everything Changed
Picture this: life before the world flipped upside down. It felt like standing in a wide-open field, with nothing but possibility stretching ahead. You know that feeling, right? When you're young, and your body moves without a second thought, every day buzzing with energy and hope.
In a small Maryland town, days were painted with laughter, horseback rides, and the easy rhythm of family life. The house was always alive—siblings running around, parents offering gentle guidance, and those comforting traditions that seem to anchor every memory.
Faith was always there, woven quietly into the background. It was something inherited, like a favorite quilt—not yet something you’d grabbed hold of for yourself.
Back then, the world just seemed manageable. Sure, school had its challenges, but nothing you couldn’t get through with a bit of determination and help from your friends. There was a love for sports—especially swimming and riding—and a real appreciation for the outdoors.
At home, Christian beliefs shaped the way things were done, but those big questions about God and purpose? They lingered quietly, never pressing for answers. Not yet, anyway.
Summers meant long days at the lake, where the water promised freedom and adventure. Think about the thrill of diving in, the rush of cold water, the laughter echoing off the shore. With friends by your side, those moments felt like they’d last forever. There was this sense of invincibility—a belief that nothing truly bad could happen. The future felt limitless. College, travel, maybe even a career in art or teaching. Everything seemed possible.
Of course, beneath the surface, there were doubts and insecurities—just the stuff that comes with growing up. Sometimes, trying to fit in or meet expectations felt like a heavy weight. There were moments when faith seemed distant, even irrelevant. But honestly, those struggles felt small compared to the excitement of simply living. The idea that everything could change in an instant? That just didn’t cross your mind.
Family was at the heart of it all. Parents encouraged independence, but were always there with guidance. Siblings brought their own mix of competition and companionship, teaching lessons about loyalty—and forgiveness. The community, too, offered a sense of belonging. Friends, neighbors, church members—they all celebrated the highs and helped weather the lows together.
Looking back now, it’s clear how those early days laid the foundation for everything that followed. The love of movement, the value of relationships, and that quiet thread of faith all became crucial when life got tough. But back then? Life was just unfolding, one ordinary day at a time, with no hint of the storm that was waiting just out of sight.
